text:
rachel: Quick triage - bringing up reranker v12 (int8) and seeing a weird pattern: NDCG up slightly (+0.6%) but MRR down ~1.9% on the ecommerce holdout. Top1 takes the hit while top3 is stable. Thoughts?

andy: That NDCG/MRR divergence often signals pairwise ordering flips near the cutoff. Do we have per-query pairwise flip rate or Kendall tau between ranks?

rachel: Uploaded quick artifacts: s3://bench/rerank/6789012345/summary.csv and s3://bench/rerank/6789012345/pairwise_deltas.jsonl

```
model,cohort,ndcg,mrr,top1,kendall_tau
float32,ec-holdout,0.621,0.502,0.52,0.912
int8,ec-holdout,0.625,0.492,0.47,0.878
```

kevin: Kendall drop is telling (0.912 -> 0.878). Two avenues: (1) quant noise compresses score gaps so pairwise order flips increase, (2) loss calibration changed during training for the new checkpoint (pairwise vspointwise). Did we swap the calibration head during bring-up?

samir: Also check whether the eval harness uses the same rerank scorer threshold/margin. We recently landed a PR that applies a small pairwise margin correction for float models; if canary missed it that explains NDCG uptick (better tail order) but MRR drop (top-1 suffers).

rachel: Confirmed: float run had postprocess pairwise_margin=0.002 (legacy) enabled; int8 run accidentally set pairwise_margin=0.0. Oof. That could be the diff.

andy: Interesting. Pairwise margin tends to stabilize top1 by pushing a tiny margin between docs. Without it, jitter can produce more top1 swaps even if global NDCG rises. Let's run three ablations on a 25k sample: (A) int8 + float pairwise_margin=0.002, (B) int8 + logit_smoothing(scale=1.01), (C) float but pairwise_margin=0.0 to see symmetric effect. Queue CI jobs.

rachel: Kicked off jobs: 6789012350 (A), 6789012361 (B), 6789012372 (C). CI: https://ci.redwood.prod/jobs/6789012350

ci-bot: Jobs queued: 6789012350, 6789012361, 6789012372

kevin: Also compute permutation test p-value for MRR difference and bootstrap 95% CI. If p<0.01 it's significant and we must block.

rachel: Early ablation peek: A (int8 + margin) recovers ~1.4% MRR on ec-holdout. B (smoothing) recovers ~0.9%. C (float without margin) drops MRR ~1.6% and increases swap_rate. Permutation test p ~0.004 (MRR gap float vs int8 baseline), bootstrap CI float MRR [0.496,0.508], int8 baseline [0.486,0.498].

andy: So primary cause was the harness postprocess flag mismatch. Two actions: (1) enforce eval-config parity guard to assert pairwise_margin equality between float and canary, (2) revert canary to enable margin and re-run full canary. Also add a canary metric 'swap_rate_top1' (fraction of queries where top1 changes).

kevin: For longer-term, let's evaluate if pairwise_margin should be part of the model checkpoint (learned) instead of a harness postprocess. It hides coupling between eval and runtime. But in short-term, CI guard + dashboard micro-slice for swap_rate is good.

samir: One nuance: margin interacts with quantization differently; when we add margin to int8 it recovered most but not all. Suggest also running mixed-last-layer ablation to quantify residual quant math effect.

rachel: Queued mixed-last-layer run job 6789012383 on a 10k subset. Also uploading per-query disagreement dump (top-5) for highest-impact queries to s3://bench/rerank/6789012345/disagreements_200.jsonl

ci-bot: Job 6789012383 queued.

kevin: After re-run, if residual MRR gap remains >0.5% we should consider tuning PTQ clipping per-layer or adding small logit scaling for int8 as a temporary mitigation for sensitive cohorts. But prefer to avoid per-cohort hand-tuning if possible.

andy: Also a quick stat note for the rollout playbook: when NDCG and MRR diverge, automatically trigger pairwise diagnostics (kendall, swap_rate, per-query gap histograms) and ablation matrix: margin parity, smoothing, mixed-last-layer. Saves time.

rachel: Agree. I'll add a PR to the harness to (a) fail canary on eval-config diffs for pairwise_margin and postprocess flags, (b) surface swap_rate_top1 and kendall in the canary dashboard, and (c) add the ablation matrix template to the reranker-onboard runbook. Ticket: RERANK-8120.

samir: Early mixed-last-layer result: recovers an extra ~0.4% MRR (so combined with margin we mostly close the gap).

kevin: Good. Proposed immediate deploy decision: re-run full canary with pairwise_margin enabled for int8 and block if MRR still >1.0% below float. If within 1.0%, allow canary progression with a mitigation note.

rachel: Re-run queued (job 6789012400). Will post final numbers. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
